results.title: Is this enough homoscedasticity for linear regression?
results.content:
Context (Post Title): Is this enough homoscedasticity for linear regression?
Comment: Homoskedasticity has *nothing* to do with the consistency of OLS estimates! OLS is consistent under correct specification with very mild assumptions (e.g. finite fourth moments of the regessors and some cross-terms). Always use Whites robust, HC3, or bootstrapped standard errors because... they are robust to heteroskedasticity of any form!
What you probably meant was, ‘does the error term seem mean-independent of the explanatory variable?’ In which case, I suggest three things. For a quick-and-dirty solution, throw in a quadratic term (`lm(Y ~ mpg + I(mpg^2), data = mydata)`). For a more flexible solution, use splines, e.g. `lm(Y ~ I(splines::bs(mpg, degree = 4)), data = mydata)`.
Finally, you could fit a fully non-parametric model on the residuals and see if it captures anything without any assumptions about the functional form (no polynomials, logarithms—nothing), e.g.

  mydata$r <- mod$residuals
  library(np)
  bwspec <- npregbw(Y ~ r, data = mydata, regtype = "ll")
  print(npsigtest(bwspec)) # To test the significance of deviations from zero

Even if you have more variables in the model, a rejection based on one non-parametric fit is an argument to make your model more flexible (maybe semi-parametric).
